Classify an ordinary differential equation

Source: R/solvers-ode-ode.R
classify_ode.Rd

classify_ode(eq, func) returns the hints, in SymPy's order, of the methods dsolve() can use to solve the ODE eq, as SymPy's classify_ode(). With dict = TRUE it returns a dictionary of the matching hints with the keys order, default and ordered_hints.

Usage

classify_ode(
  eq,
  func = NULL,
  dict = FALSE,
  ics = NULL,
  prep = TRUE,
  xi = NULL,
  eta = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

eq

The equation.

func

The unknown function; detected when NULL.

dict

Whether to return the dictionary of matches.

ics

Initial conditions, as for dsolve().

prep

Whether to preprocess the equation.

xi, eta

Infinitesimals for the lie_group hint.

n

The number of power series terms.

...

Further options: hint and x0.

Value

A character vector of hints, or a dictionary.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x"); f <- Function("f")
classify_ode(Derivative(f(x), x) - f(x), f(x))
#>  [1] "separable"                            
#>  [2] "1st_exact"                            
#>  [3] "1st_linear"                           
#>  [4] "Bernoulli"                            
#>  [5] "almost_linear"                        
#>  [6] "1st_power_series"                     
#>  [7] "lie_group"                            
#>  [8] "nth_linear_constant_coeff_homogeneous"
#>  [9] "separable_Integral"                   
#> [10] "1st_exact_Integral"                   
#> [11] "1st_linear_Integral"                  
#> [12] "Bernoulli_Integral"                   
#> [13] "almost_linear_Integral"
